primary_meaning: In mainstream Christian teaching, 'stone' (and the closely related 'rock') most commonly symbolizes Jesus Christ himself, especially as the rejected stone that becomes the cornerstone/foundation of God's building (the church), and simultaneously as a stone of stumbling for unbelievers. The New Testament writers explicitly apply the Old Testament 'stone' texts christologically, and this reading has been dominant from the patristic era onward.
primary_basis: Psalm 118:22 (the stone the builders rejected has become the cornerstone)
Isaiah 28:16 (a tested, precious cornerstone laid in Zion)
Isaiah 8:14 (a stone of stumbling, a rock of offense)
Daniel 2:34-35, 44-45 (the stone cut without hands that destroys the statue and becomes a great mountain, read christologically/messianically)
Romans 9:32-33 (stumbling stone in Zion applied to Christ)
1 Peter 2:4-8 (the living stone, cornerstone, and stone of stumbling all applied to Christ)
1 Corinthians 10:4 (the rock that followed Israel was Christ)

alternatives.meaning: Believers as 'living stones' built into a spiritual house/temple upon Christ the cornerstone \u2014 the church as God's building.
God himself as 'the Rock' \u2014 a title of stability, refuge, and faithfulness (often merged with the christological reading but originally a divine epithet).

Peter as the rock on which the church is built \u2014 dominant in Roman Catholic interpretation; Protestant traditions often read the rock as Peter's confession or as Christ, making this a materially contested reading.
Stones as memorials or witnesses \u2014 standing stones, altars, and cairns commemorating covenant events (Bethel, Gilgal, Ebenezer).
Stone as hardness/deadness of the human heart, contrasted with a heart of flesh in regeneration.
Stone tablets of the Law \u2014 stone representing the old covenant written externally, contrasted with the Spirit writing on hearts.
The 'white stone' with a new name given to the overcomer \u2014 variously read as acquittal, admission (tessera), or personal acceptance by Christ; no agreed interpretation.

The Daniel 2 stone read specifically as the kingdom of God (rather than Christ personally) crushing worldly empires \u2014 emphasized in some eschatological traditions (e.g., historicist and Latter-day Saint readings).

notes: Consensus is strong because the New Testament itself performs the interpretation: Jesus, Peter, and Paul all quote the Old Testament stone texts (Psalm 118:22; Isaiah 8:14; 28:16) and apply them directly to Christ, and 1 Peter 2:4-8 gathers all three into a single christological catena. The main genuine interpretive divergence concerns Matthew 16:18 (Peter vs. Peter's confession vs. Christ), which is a confessional dividing line rather than a challenge to the broader Christ-as-cornerstone consensus. Secondary meanings (living stones, memorial stones, stony hearts, tablets of law) are widely acknowledged but treated as distinct sub-motifs rather than rivals to the primary meaning.
